chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Basir, from Imam Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) who said:

Imam Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) said: "Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, did not establish for people a proof against themselves except through the manifestation of the Imam. So when the Imam manifests and establishes the proof, then if he dies or is killed, the people have no proof against themselves after him until the other Imam manifests."
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for divine proof being established against humanity according to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In Shia theology, this narration from Kamal al-Din underscores the concept of 'Istidlal' (establishing the proof), where the Imam serves as the definitive divine argument for humanity. It clarifies that accountability is not suspended during the interval between Imams, as the previous Imam's establishment of proof remains valid until the successor manifests, ensuring continuous divine guidance.
